shortDescription: Swiss drugmaker Novartis BX:NOT on Tuesday said a late-stage study assessing drug del-desiran's impact on myotonic dystrophy, a form of muscle wasting, had not met its target on a key metric, but reaffirmed its sales guidance through 2030.Novartis said in a statement that the Phase III HARBOR study…

children: on Tuesday said a late-stage study assessing drug del-desiran's impact on myotonic dystrophy, a form of muscle wasting, had not met its target on a key metric, but reaffirmed its sales guidance through 2030.

Novartis said in a statement that the Phase III HARBOR study "did not demonstrate statistically significant improvement versus placebo on the primary endpoint of video hand opening time", a measure of hand myotonia.

Shreeram Aradhye, President of Development and Chief Medical Officer at Novartis, said that developing therapies for a disease like myotonic dystrophy type 1 remains challenging, and that setbacks are part of scientific progress.

The company's announcement came a day after shares in Novartis fell by more than 3% on news that its cholesterol drug failed in a closely watched study, dealing a blow to what investors had seen as a blockbuster treatment.
Novartis said it was sticking to its guidance that sales would grow at a compound annual rate of 5-6% from 2025 to 2030.
